name: run_shell
description: Execute a command with platform-aware safety controls. You can pass either `command` (for short one-line commands like `git status --short`) or `program` plus `args` (for exact argv control). By default no shell interpreter is invoked: shell metacharacters like `;`, `&&`, `|`, redirection, command substitution, and background operators are rejected in `command` to prevent accidental shell-style composition. When real shell syntax is required, set `shell` explicitly; shell mode is rejected in Restricted shell access and only works in ConfirmAll/Open. In the default restricted mode, only whitelisted commands are allowed: python/python3, pip/pip3 (normalized to python -m pip), node/npm/npx, read-only git, and scoped filesystem commands like pwd/ls/cat/mkdir/cp/mv. Simple filesystem commands are implemented natively by the app, so use them directly for directory creation, copying, and moving instead of writing one-off Python snippets. For plain-text read/create/edit/list work, prefer read_file, read_files, create_file, edit_file, and list_dir over Python. Reserve Python for real scripts, structured document workflows, parsing/transforms, or operations that need libraries. Do not pass `command` together with `program` or `args`; shell mode also must not be combined with program/args. For large scripts or generated text, pass the content through `stdin` and use a program form that reads stdin (for example python with args ["-"]); do not stuff large content into argv. For HTML-first PPTX/deck generation, call the renderer with `--spec -` and put the generated JSON spec in `stdin`; never put raw HTML/CSS/JSON deck specs inside `args` or `python -c`. If the user loosens shell access in Settings, arbitrary bare commands may be allowed, with optional per-call confirmation. Output is capped at 64 KB per stream. Default timeout 30s; set timeout_secs to 0 only when a long-running install/download/build is intentional and should not have a per-command timeout. The broader agent turn timeout can still stop the run unless Settings disables or raises it. For Windows paths in JSON strings, escape backslashes (for example "E:\\Starting\\script.py") or use forward slashes.

command.description: Simple one-line command string. Without shell, it is parsed into argv without invoking a shell. Use this for ordinary commands like "git status --short" or "python -m pytest". Quotes and escaped spaces are supported for arguments, but shell operators such as ;, &&, |, >, <, `...`, $(...), and backgrounding are rejected unless shell is explicitly set. On Windows, path backslashes are preserved by the command parser; JSON strings still need escaped backslashes such as "C:\\Users\\me\\script.py". Do not provide command together with program or args.

shell.description: Optional explicit shell mode for command. false/none/direct means no shell. true/default uses PowerShell on Windows and sh on Unix-like systems. powershell uses Windows PowerShell on Windows or pwsh elsewhere; pwsh uses PowerShell Core; cmd is Windows-only; bash uses bash -lc; sh uses sh -c. Shell mode permits shell syntax such as &&, pipes, redirects, variables, and command substitution, but is rejected in Restricted shell access mode and should only be used when shell interpretation is intentional.

program.description: Program to execute when not using command. In restricted mode it must be one of: python, python3, pip, pip3, node, npm, npx, git, pwd, ls, cat, mkdir, cp, mv. pwd/ls/cat/mkdir/cp/mv run natively inside the app and work even when the OS has no matching external binary. pip/pip3 are normalized to python/python3 -m pip. Simple aliases copy->cp and move->mv are also accepted. In less-restricted shell access modes, any bare command name may be allowed. No shell interpreter is invoked automatically.

args.description: Arguments passed directly as argv when using program (no shell interpretation). Defaults to []. Do not use args with command. For generated HTML/PPTX specs, use args like [".../edit_doc.py", "--path", ".../deck.pptx", "create_html_pptx", "--spec", "-", "--outdir", ".../html_deck_project", "--mode", "hybrid", "--screenshot", "auto"] and put the JSON spec in stdin. In restricted mode, git first arg must be a read-only subcommand (status, diff, log, show, ls-files, rev-parse, branch, tag, config, remote, describe, blame), and filesystem-command paths are resolved relative to cwd and must stay inside registered source roots.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command. In restricted mode it must resolve inside a registered source directory. In less-restricted shell access modes, any existing directory may be allowed.

timeout_secs.description: Timeout in seconds. Default 30. Set 0 for no per-command timeout when a long install/download/build is intentional. The broader agent turn timeout can still stop the run if it is not raised or disabled.

stdin.description: Optional text written to the child process stdin. Use this for scripts or generated content that would exceed argv limits, e.g. program python with args ["-"] and stdin containing the script. For HTML-first PPTX generation, pass the JSON deck spec here while using --spec - in args. The payload is bounded and is not logged. Native filesystem commands do not accept stdin.
